lines: Route 10's back to its regular amount of chaos. Best kind.
Well, would you look at that. Go find his person before he changes his mind about the whole arrangement.
Sounds like you're closing in. My money's always been on the mill pond — every dog in this county ends up there eventually.
Down at Cellar Door too? That dog's putting on some miles. Try Middle Brook next — Dot doesn't miss much.
Head down toward Hobart first — I heard Cellar Door had a sighting.
Have you seen the flyers? Somebody's dog got loose a few days back — sweet thing, fast as anything.
Half the county's spotted him by now and nobody's caught him yet.
If you're headed out today, keep an eye open — every sighting helps.
Glad that one has a happy ending. Come back for a tasting sometime, once things settle down.
There he is! Knew he'd turn up looking pleased with himself.
Told you — trotted right through here like he owned the patio. Middle Brook's your next stop.
Oh, the escape artist! He came through the patio yesterday like he owned the place,
then vanished off toward the scenic trail before anyone could grab a leash.
Welcome — pull up a seat on the patio anytime.
Bet he's back home causing a whole new kind of trouble. Good.
You got him?! Bring him by — everyone in here's been rooting for you all week.
Try the mill pond, past the inn. Dogs love that shade by the water.
Oh, the dog! He was right outside our window yesterday, plain as day, gone before anyone could grab him.
If I were you, I'd try the mill pond — there's shade by the water and dogs love that spot on a warm day.
Heard Cellar Door had a sighting too — small world. Try there if you haven't yet.
Big week around here — ask Earl down at Stewart's in Stamford, he'll fill you in.
Still can't believe it. Thank you again — I mean it about the coffee.
Scout?! Oh — oh, thank you, I've been up and down this road for two days.
Come by Stamford Coffee sometime — coffee's on me. I mean that.

effects.toast: Episode complete — new story next week

lines: Have you seen a scruffy little guy, answers to Scout — well, doesn't answer to Scout, that's rather the problem?
I'm starting to think he's doing this on purpose.
A scruffy dog is sprawled in the shade by the mill pond, thoroughly pleased with himself.
He trots straight over like he'd been expecting you the whole time.
A hand-drawn flyer taped inside the window: LOST DOG — SCOUT. ANSWERS TO NOTHING. LAST SEEN EVERYWHERE.
A flyer on the corkboard by the register, same dog, a new hand-written line underneath: "still out here having the time of his life."
Taped to the door: the same LOST DOG flyer, with a little pencil sketch someone's added of a dog wearing sunglasses.
Chalkboard by the tavern door: pizza night Monday and Wednesday. Someone's chalked a small paw print in the corner, for luck.
